cmd: browser-pilot do "Open http://127.0.0.1:4180/ and sign in with email «redacted» and password «redacted». Then create a new ticket titled exactly 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (fill in any other required fields with sensible values). After submitting, wait for the list/detail view to refresh (it updates a short beat after the mutation, not instantly) and confirm the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' now exists. Report the confirmation text or the ticket row/detail you observed, including the ticket's initial status." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 30

browser-pilot do "On the repair-desk app, open the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (ref RD-1015) and add a part named exactly 'scref3 RD Part A' with cost 100 and markup 25. Fill any other required fields sensibly. After saving, wait for the view to refresh (it updates a short beat after the mutation, not instantly) and confirm the part appears on the ticket. Report the price the app computes for this part (the exact value shown on the page), plus any other computed totals shown." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 30

browser-pilot do "On the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (ref RD-1015), add a second part named exactly 'scref3 RD Part B' with cost 200 and markup 25. Fill any other required fields sensibly. After saving, wait for the view to refresh (it updates a short beat after the mutation, not instantly) and confirm both parts are listed on the ticket: 'scref3 RD Part A' and 'scref3 RD Part B'. Report the price the app computes for 'scref3 RD Part B' (exact value shown), and the prices shown for both parts." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 30

browser-pilot do "On the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (ref RD-1015), edit the part 'scref3 RD Part A' so its cost changes from 100 to 150 (keep markup at 25 and quantity as it was). Save the change, wait for the view to refresh (it updates a short beat after the mutation, not instantly), and confirm the part now shows cost 150. Report the price the app computes for 'scref3 RD Part A' afterwards (exact value shown on the page), and the ticket's parts total." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 30

browser-pilot do "On the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (ref RD-1015), the goal is to get the ticket's status to 'Ready'. The app enforces preconditions before it will accept that status — attempt the status change to Ready, read any error/validation message the app shows, discover what the preconditions are, satisfy them (e.g. filling required fields, intermediate statuses, or other requirements the app demands), and retry until the ticket's status is actually 'Ready' as shown on the page. Do NOT delete or remove the parts. Report: (a) the exact precondition error/validation text the app showed, (b) exactly what you had to do to satisfy each precondition, and (c) the final status shown on the page." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 40

browser-pilot do "On the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (ref RD-1015), which is currently in status Ready: (1) remove/delete both parts 'scref3 RD Part A' and 'scref3 RD Part B' from the ticket — after each delete, wait for the view to refresh (it updates a short beat after the mutation, not instantly) and confirm the part is gone before moving on; (2) then archive the ticket (use the app's archive action; if the app blocks archiving, read the error, satisfy what it requires, and retry). Finally verify the ticket is archived and no longer appears in the active/open tickets list, and that no parts remain on it. Report: the confirmation text shown for each part deletion, the confirmation text for archiving, where the ticket now lives (e.g. archived list), and the ticket's final status." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 40

browser-pilot do "Verify the end state of the repair-desk app: (1) confirm the ticket 'scref3 RD Bench Ticket' (RD-1015) does NOT appear in the active (non-archived) ticket list — check with 'Show archived' unchecked; (2) confirm that when archived tickets are shown, RD-1015 appears with an Archived badge, status Ready, and 0 parts; (3) confirm no parts named 'scref3 RD Part A' or 'scref3 RD Part B' exist anywhere on that ticket. Report exactly what you observed for each of the three checks." --session scref3 --json --max-turns 25

finalText:
All objectives completed and verified. Final report:

**1. DONE** — Ticket `scref3 RD Bench Ticket` created (ref **RD-1015**, customer "Bench Customer"), initial status **Draft**.

**2. DONE** — Part `scref3 RD Part A` added with cost 100 and markup 25. App-computed price: **$125.00** (100 × 1.25).

**3. DONE** — Part `scref3 RD Part B` added with cost 200 and markup 25. App-computed price: **$250.00** (200 × 1.25). Parts total at that point: $375.00.

**4. DONE** — Part A's cost changed from 100 to 150 (markup still 25). App-computed price afterwards: **$187.50** (150 × 1.25). Ticket parts total became $437.50.

**5. DONE** — Ticket ended in status **Ready**. Precondition discovered: the app rejected the status change with the exact error — *"Ticket is not ready. Part "scref3 RD Part A" has no supplier. Part "scref3 RD Part B" has no supplier."* What was required: **every part on the ticket must have a supplier assigned**. I satisfied this by editing Part A to add supplier "ABC Supplies" and Part B to add supplier "XYZ Parts Inc.", after which the status change to Ready was accepted and the page showed status **Ready**.

**6. DONE** — Both parts removed (after deleting Part A the table showed only Part B; after deleting Part B the table showed "No parts on this ticket yet."), then the ticket was archived via the "Archive ticket" button (button changed to "Unarchive ticket"). Final verification: with "Show archived" unchecked, RD-1015 is absent from the active list (active tickets run RD-1014 down to RD-1004); with archived shown, RD-1015 appears with an **Archived** badge, status **Ready**, **0 parts**. Nothing created by this run remains active.
